publications.title: Description-Guided CLIP (Ye et al., 2026)
publications.verificationNotes: Exact title, venue, datasets/versions, prompt and shot setup, split design, metric calculation, and calibration procedure must be verified from the paper. Do not quote these numbers as established facts until checked.
publications.relevanceNote: Project notes report Description-Guided CLIP results: 16-shot accuracy of 93.16% on PlantVillage, 79.30% on Cassava, 96.56% on Pear, and 56.96% on 21-class PlantDoc cross-domain evaluation. The notes distinguish local evidence calibration from conventional confidence calibration.

publications.title: BLAP (Xiong et al., 2026)
publications.verificationNotes: Full title, dataset composition, metrics, split design, field-test protocol, and exact meaning of the reported results are unverified. A 36-image test cannot by itself establish broad field generalisation.
publications.relevanceNote: Project notes describe BLAP as involving 990 images, 11 crops, 33 categories, reported 92.78% accuracy, and a 360-image wheat-field evaluation with 36/36 test images reportedly correct. The notes also associate the work with OOD, leave-one-crop-out, severity, and recommendation validation.

publications.title: Leakage or session splits (Kang, 2026)
publications.verificationNotes: The exact paper, dataset, sensor-reading definition, overlap method, and result are unverified. Confirm that the study concerns the relevant crop-disease dataset.
publications.relevanceNote: Project notes report a result that 91.9% of CDD test images share sensor readings with training images, motivating session/farm-disjoint evaluation.

publications.title: AgriPath-LF16 (Mooraj et al., 2026)
publications.verificationNotes: Dataset release, version, image count, class distribution, field provenance, licensing, and split metadata are unverified.
publications.relevanceNote: AgriPath-LF16 was discussed as a possible field-oriented dataset lead; project notes mention 111,000 images, 16 crops, and 41 diseases.

publications.title: CCMT crop-disease image dataset
publications.abstract: The CCMT data paper presents crop pest and disease images sourced from local farms in Ghana. It describes 24,881 raw images (cashew 6,549; cassava 7,508; maize 5,389; tomato 5,435) and a separate augmented collection of 102,976 images across 22 categories. The paper describes expert annotation and review.
publications.verificationNotes: Title, journal, year, DOI and abstract-level dataset counts checked against the Data in Brief record. The raw and augmented collections are distinct; do not treat augmented images as independent original observations. Source-image lineage, duplicate overlap and split-level leakage still require direct dataset audit.
publications.relevanceNote: A Ghanaian crop-disease dataset candidate with raw and augmented collections. Useful for a Ghana-grounded experiment if original-image provenance, class labels, licence and split lineage support leakage-resistant evaluation.

publications.title: Neuro-symbolic AI for rice disease diagnosis with calibrated attention and rule-aware explanations
publications.abstract: The study evaluates a ResNet-34+CBAM rice-disease classifier with post-hoc probability calibration and an RDF/OWL rule-aware validator on a deduplicated PaddyDoctor split. It reports 95.13% accuracy and 95.14% weighted F1. Temperature scaling slightly improves test Brier score and NLL but increases test ECE from 0.82% to 0.94%. Corruption testing reports large performance drops under brightness shift and Gaussian blur.
publications.verificationNotes: Article page and abstract checked; available online 11 February 2026, In Press/Corrected Proof at time of review. DOI verified. The article states that further validation across seasons, devices and geographic regions is needed. This catalogue has not independently rerun the reported experiments.
publications.relevanceNote: Directly relevant precedent: calibration, data deduplication, AURC/risk-coverage and field-relevant corruption analysis already exist on PaddyDoctor. It narrows the thesis toward external-domain calibration/selective-prediction transfer rather than claiming calibration itself is novel.
publications.researchMethod: ResNet-34 with CBAM; SHA-256 and perceptual-hash deduplication; temperature scaling; ECE, Brier, NLL, AURC and corruption evaluation; post-hoc RDF/OWL rule validation.
publications.keyFindings: 95.13% accuracy; 95.14% weighted F1; test ECE 0.82% before and 0.94% after temperature scaling; Brier 0.0760 to 0.0758; NLL 0.1573 to 0.1566; severe brightness and blur sensitivity.
publications.limitations: Single PaddyDoctor corpus; article explicitly calls for evaluation across seasons, devices and geographic regions. Corruption tests do not replace external validation.

publications.title: PALM-Net: Population-aware leaf disease multilinear network for robust plant disease detection
publications.venue: Journal of King Saud University Computer and Information Sciences
publications.abstract: PALM-Net proposes a population-aware multilinear learning framework intended to improve plant disease recognition under laboratory and real-field variability. It evaluates PlantVillage, Cassava Leaf Disease and Tomato Disease datasets and reports Top-1 accuracy of 99.32%, 84.56% and 97.44%, respectively.
publications.datasetOrArtifact: PlantVillage; Cassava Leaf Disease; Tomato Disease
publications.verificationNotes: Publisher article page and abstract checked; published 18 November 2026. DOI, journal, volume and article number verified. The abstract/source extract emphasises accuracy, feature representation and model efficiency; do not infer that calibration or selective prediction were evaluated unless confirmed in the full text.
publications.relevanceNote: Recent multi-dataset and field-robustness precedent. It means the thesis should not claim that cross-dataset field performance has never been investigated. The candidate distinction is calibrated confidence and selective risk under independently defined domain shifts.
publications.researchMethod: Population-aware multilinear learning with multi-scale attentive leaf features, population-level feature purification and factorised classification head.
publications.keyFindings: Reported Top-1 accuracy: 99.32% PlantVillage, 84.56% Cassava and 97.44% Tomato.
publications.limitations: The available abstract does not establish a cross-domain calibration/selective-prediction protocol or external geographic validation beyond the reported datasets.

publications.title: Vision-driven retrieval-augmented decision support for plant disease diagnosis using EfficientNetV2 and large language models
publications.abstract: EffiToRag integrates an EfficientNetV2 visual diagnosis module with retrieval-augmented generation. Predicted disease classes are used to retrieve relevant records from a structured agronomic knowledge base. The paper reports a held-out test set of 11,621 images across 60 plant-health classes, 99.13% accuracy and 0.9889 Macro F1 for EfficientNetV2-M.
publications.verificationNotes: Scientific Reports article page checked; published 18 November 2026. DOI and listed authors verified. Treat reported performance as the authors’ held-out CDDM result, not evidence of external geographic/device generalisation.
publications.relevanceNote: Shows that visual diagnosis and knowledge-grounded recommendations are already being integrated. It is not a direct calibration study in the checked abstract and is not a directly comparable model unless task and dataset protocols are aligned.
publications.researchMethod: EfficientNetV2 visual diagnosis, class-aware augmentation/training and retrieval-augmented generation over an agronomic knowledge base.
publications.keyFindings: 11,621 held-out images, 60 plant-health classes; 99.13% accuracy and 0.9889 Macro F1 reported for EfficientNetV2-M.
publications.limitations: The abstract reports held-out benchmark performance and knowledge-retrieval evaluation; it does not establish calibration transfer across independent field domains.

publications.title: ARTEN-Enhanced Multi-Crop Disease Dataset: A Large-Scale High-Resolution Agricultural Image Resource for Plant Disease Analysis and Artificial Intelligence Applications
publications.abstract: The ARTEN-enhanced dataset provides a computationally derived representation of a previously published multi-crop disease dataset. It retains 21,875 source images and their biological categories, covers five crop species and 30 healthy/disease classes, and introduces no new field observations. The paper reports image-quality measures including PSNR and SSIM and notes that these do not independently establish preservation of disease-specific features.
publications.datasetOrArtifact: ARTEN-Enhanced Multi-Crop Disease Dataset; source dataset DOI 10.17632/6243z8r6t6.1; enhanced dataset DOI 10.17632/s2sxywhtx5.1
publications.verificationNotes: Scientific Data article page and abstract checked; published 19 November 2026. DOI and authors verified. This is a derived image dataset, not a new independent field collection.
publications.relevanceNote: Important dataset-provenance caution: enhanced images are derived from existing source images and should not be counted as an independent external field domain. The paper itself distinguishes image-quality similarity from diagnostic/biological preservation.
publications.researchMethod: Agricultural Residual Texture Enhancement Network (ARTEN) applied to an existing multi-crop image collection.
publications.keyFindings: 21,875 enhanced images; five crop species; 30 healthy/disease classes; reported mean PSNR 37.98 dB and SSIM 0.9768.
publications.limitations: No new field observations were collected. PSNR/SSIM and bounding-box analyses do not establish lesion-level or diagnostic preservation; the article calls for further lesion-level and pathology validation.

publications.title: SAGE: Scalable Agentic Grounded Evaluation for Crop Disease Diagnosis
publications.venue: CVPR 2026 Workshop on Emerging Directions in Data for Multimodal Foundation Models (DataMFM; non-archival track)
publications.abstract: SAGE combines a large plant-disease image collection (approximately 839,000 images, 335 crops and 1,251 disease classes) with source-grounded symptom knowledge and a training-free agentic visual reasoning pipeline. The project page reports an average 16.2 percentage-point accuracy improvement from symptom knowledge at the full reference budget across four evaluation crops.
publications.datasetOrArtifact: SAGE image/symptom collection and source-cited disease knowledge base
publications.verificationNotes: Author project page, arXiv record and workshop acceptance statement checked. Accepted at the CVPR 2026 DataMFM workshop in a non-archival track; do not describe it as a conventional archival conference proceedings paper.
publications.relevanceNote: Important adjacent work on agentic visual diagnosis and source-grounded symptom knowledge. It broadens the status quo beyond CNN classifiers, but it is not directly equivalent to a calibrated closed-set classifier.
publications.researchMethod: Training-free visual-language/agentic diagnosis using anatomical context, source-grounded symptom descriptions and sequential reference-image comparison.
publications.keyFindings: Approximately 839K images, 335 crops, 1,251 disease classes; reported mean 16.2 percentage-point improvement from symptom knowledge at full reference budget.
publications.limitations: Workshop contribution is non-archival. The project page does not establish the cross-domain confidence calibration and selective-risk evaluation proposed here.

publications.title: A Weekly Multi-Modal Dataset of Soil Physicochemical Parameters, Environmental Conditions, Irrigation Records, Crop Growth Observations, Harvest Parameters, and Field Images from Six Cowpea and Maize Varieties in Sumbrungu, Bolgatanga, Ghana
publications.abstract: A 15-week field-trial dataset from Sumbrungu Experimental Farm, Bolgatanga, Ghana, covering six cowpea and maize varieties, soil and environmental measurements, irrigation records, crop growth and harvest parameters, and field photographs from Weeks 3–12.
publications.datasetOrArtifact: Ghana LSACROFT Sumbrungu Experimental Farm dataset, Version 1
publications.verificationNotes: Mendeley Data record checked; published 22 September 2026, Version 1, CC BY 4.0. The public description does not identify disease labels or disease annotations; inspect the actual files before any further use.
publications.relevanceNote: Provides Ghanaian field-trial context and field images, but the available description does not establish disease labels. It is not a supervised crop-disease recognition benchmark without additional validated annotations.
publications.researchMethod: Weekly multi-modal field trial using a Randomised Complete Block Design with three replications and a control treatment.
publications.keyFindings: Six crop varieties; 15-week growing season from 14 March to 26 June 2026; field photographs reported for Weeks 3–12.
publications.limitations: The dataset description is for crop growth and field monitoring, not labelled plant disease diagnosis.
